transcript.speaker: p-beth
transcript.text: Okay, I think we have most people. Let's get started, and Lukas can catch up when he joins. I'll go around by subsystem, same order as last week.

transcript.speaker: p-omar
transcript.text: Can I just say, uh, I think the shared tracker is out of date for a few of these, so if something looks wrong in the rows, say so.

transcript.speaker: p-ingrid
transcript.text: Understood. Start with actuators, Arjun.

transcript.speaker: p-arjun
transcript.text: ok so knee actuator, the new batch of housings passed the leak check, no weeps. the encoder cal is still the long pole, we redo it per unit and its slow. i think we can get it down if jonas gives us the batch script

transcript.speaker: p-jonas
transcript.text: script is mostly done, ill push it today

transcript.speaker: p-arjun
transcript.text: great ty. and the hip one, dmitri has more on that

transcript.speaker: p-dmitri
transcript.text: Right. Dyno is booked solid through the week. We saw the housing temp climb faster than the model on the long holds. I don't want to call it until I've seen two more runs!!

transcript.speaker: p-ingrid
transcript.text: Is that a cooling problem or a controls problem? I don't want to chase the wrong one.

transcript.speaker: p-dmitri
transcript.text: Don't know yet. Could be the thermal pad contact. Could be the current limit on the drive being looser than we assumed.

transcript.speaker: p-priya
transcript.text: To answer Ingrid's question from the legs side: 1. The leg structure hasn't changed, so cooling is not coming from us. 2. We did change the pad thickness on the last revision. 3. I'd want that checked before anyone blames the drive.

transcript.speaker: p-farah
transcript.text: On the electrical side, I can confirm the drive current limit is set where we said. 1. Limit verified on the bench. 2. Logging is a bit noisy. 3. I'd like a fresh capture on the dyno.

transcript.speaker: p-dmitri
transcript.text: Fine, Farah, send me what you want logged and I'll add it.

transcript.speaker: p-sofia
transcript.text: Hands update. Finger tendon routing is stable after the last rework. We're still seeing a creak on the wrist joint at the end of travel, and Lukas's team may need to look at the housing.

transcript.speaker: p-lukas
transcript.text: sorry late. yep ok

transcript.speaker: p-ingrid
transcript.text: Lukas, anything from structures before we get to schedule?

transcript.speaker: p-lukas
transcript.text: wrist housing is on the cmm, results tmrw. torso brackets ok

transcript.speaker: p-nora
transcript.text: From manufacturing, to restate the question, are we confident the parts for the next builds are showing up on time. Honestly, 1. most of it is. 2. a couple of fasteners are still short. 3. I'd like Gwen to confirm.

transcript.speaker: p-gwen
transcript.text: Fasteners are being expedited. I'll post the status in the channel after this, I don't have it in front of me.

transcript.speaker: p-omar
transcript.text: Hm, sorry, can you repeat that? Audio cut out. Is it the fasteners or the washers?

transcript.speaker: p-gwen
transcript.text: Both, but the fasteners matter more.

transcript.speaker: p-ingrid
transcript.text: Okay. Beth, let's get the schedule updates.

transcript.speaker: p-beth
transcript.text: So, schedule, and just to restate, the question is what moved this week. The Leg DVT build slid to 11/4, and the reason is the parts we just talked about. Everything downstream shifts by the same amount.

transcript.speaker: p-priya
transcript.text: That works for legs. 1. We can use the extra time on the hip bracket fit. 2. I'd rather not lose the gain from fixing the pad. 3. We'll need the dyno data before that.

transcript.speaker: p-ingrid
transcript.text: Is anyone worried about the test lab being the bottleneck in that window?

transcript.speaker: p-dmitri
transcript.text: We'll make it work. Just give me the build list early!!

transcript.speaker: p-omar
transcript.text: I think, probably, it will be fine, not 100% sure about the cal fixtures though

transcript.speaker: p-beth
transcript.text: Noted. I'll put that on the risk list.

transcript.speaker: p-beth
transcript.text: Last item on my list. The Hip actuator thermal derate at continuous torque test is now 10/12, previous date has passed. Arjun, that's consistent with what you said earlier?

transcript.speaker: p-arjun
transcript.text: yeah thats what i have, oh wait, i said thurs earlier but its the following mon, 10/12, sorry

transcript.speaker: p-ingrid
transcript.text: Fine. Any other schedule risks anyone's sitting on?

transcript.speaker: p-jonas
transcript.text: no

transcript.speaker: p-lukas
transcript.text: no

transcript.speaker: p-beth
transcript.text: Then I'll send the notes. Thanks everyone.

summary.overview: Weekly hardware program review, 54 min. Subsystem round of updates: knee actuator housings passed leak check, encoder cal still slow, hip actuator housing temps running ahead of the model on long holds with cooling vs drive limit still open. Schedule changes covered at the end.

hip act: housing temp climbing faster than model; pad contact vs current limit unresolved, need 2 more dyno runs
legs: pad thickness changed on last rev, check before blaming drive
electrical: drive limit verified on bench, wants fresh dyno capture
hands: tendon routing stable, wrist creak at end of travel, housing on CMM
fasteners short, being expedited (Gwen to post status)
Leg DVT build now 11/4, downstream shifts same amount
Hip actuator thermal derate at continuous torque now 10/12
